feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond web scale, and slightly overstuffed with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines communications leadership, CMS/platform expertise, analytics, and multimedia in a way that feels differentiated.  
- Generally high writing quality: concise, professional tone with strong action verbs and good readability.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include results such as engagement growth, email performance, cost savings, team size, campaign wins, or efficiency gains.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve focus and save space.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency fixes: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in bullets and list formatting. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the experience section, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it with sharper phrasing and one clearer differentiator would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV style.
- Add a stronger seniority cue tied to recent work, e.g., “leading digital strategy and platform modernization for mission-driven and membership organizations.”
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter formulation such as “multi-channel digital communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable complex teams to communicate effectively. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful here, but avoid repeating similar mission/advocacy language elsewhere in the header.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Consolidate overlapping workflow items: combine “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one clearer competency.
- Align style and parallel structure across all items; use either noun phrases or leadership-focused labels consistently.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Digital governance & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “stakeholder coordination,” “advocacy messaging”).
- Repeats Topline Skills and Soft Skills; consider shortening this section or removing softer items like stakeholder coordination.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo roles and Recent Projects. Make it more outcome-led and emphasize what is new at the consultant level.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + level: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, users supported, workflow improvements, search accuracy/engagement gains, reduced publishing time, fewer support issues.
- Rephrase for seniority and distinctiveness: “Led AI-enabled search strategy spanning retrieval design, structured content modeling and user discovery experience” and “Built Drupal campaign experiences and reusable content modules for member-facing initiatives.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording repeats website governance, analytics, Drupal, and cross-channel operations already covered in the Director role.
- Microsites, anniversary campaign, advocacy video, and AI search are also echoed in Recent Projects; avoid restating the same examples here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational scope, and the most senior differentiators rather than repeating channel management already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine scope + flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add metrics for email/social growth, video output, cost savings, production speed, reporting adoption, or governance efficiency.
- Tighten remaining bullets to senior-level wins: built first in-house broadcast studio; expanded analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery); formalized governance and publishing standards.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as scaling in-house production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, repeatability, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show program-building impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more outcome-oriented: “Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and campaign coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated terms tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, information architecture & content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Mission-driven stakeholder communications” if targeting broader digital leadership roles.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused.”
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof for experience bullets rather than this skills list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this list as a concise summary, not a repeat.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal specifics like “jQuery” here; keep detailed languages/frameworks in “Technical + IT.”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “public-sector web platform modernization” to align with recent NACo work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid listing the same tools at the same level of detail in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or shorten here.

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing terms: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and SEO analysis,” “insight-driven optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, performance analysis and conversion optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add context on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to another item only if you’ve used it meaningfully in production.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want stronger impact, split by proficiency/relevance: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | Working knowledge: Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller version in one place and shorten the other.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent experience, so avoid repeating it without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/strength signals instead of version labels: **Front-end development for Drupal-based sites, API integrations, tag management, edge/serverless scripting, and deployment automation**
- Consider dropping **HTML5/CSS3** to **HTML/CSS** for concision; keep only tools you’ve used recently enough to defend in interview.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or make this one more implementation-focused.
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless you specifically want this section to signal hands-on technical setup.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more role-relevant by emphasizing automation/build tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to prioritize systems you likely configured or used to build workflows: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move general collaboration tools out unless they were administered at a systems level; if kept, group separately: “Collaboration: Slack • Teams”
- Consider a sharper title: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems”
- If accurate, add scope in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack • Teams” duplicates general workplace familiarity rather than distinctive technical skill.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same language verbatim.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email platform ownership rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter and audience engagement operations**
- If accurate, add scope in a parenthetical for strongest recent relevance: **(managed high-volume member communications/newsletters reaching tens of thousands)**
- Keep only platforms you’ve directly administered or configured; order by most recent/most advanced use, likely **Dynamics 365 → Higher Logic → Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications claims in Core Competencies and Work Experience; avoid adding generic phrases like “multi-channel communications.”
- Don’t restate newsletter scale here if it already appears prominently in recent experience bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team formation, early platform/content wins, and any scale or output metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground promotion and scope: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams/videos produced, email/social volume supported, or team size/mentorship scope.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked channels: “Improved workflows across web, email, social, and video; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestream and weekly video content.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team. Improved workflows across web, email, social and video; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later operations/governance themes; keep this lighter here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it shorter, emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator, and add any scale or output metrics if available.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated research and innovation projects supporting NACo program and policy initiatives.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout result: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific deliverable or channel if possible.
- If you have numbers, add them: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, projects coordinated, or audience/download growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item centered on research/innovation support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating leadership language better demonstrated in 2018–2024 roles.
